# Overview

This notebook produces two supplementary odds-ratio tables for the leadership LCA
manuscript, both using **C3 Active constructive** as the reference profile.

| Output | Description | Section |
|---|---|---|
| **Table U** | Unadjusted ML three-step ORs (one covariate at a time, ref = C3) | *Unadjusted ORs* |
| **Table A** | Adjusted ML three-step ORs (all 8 covariates simultaneously, ref = C3) | *Adjusted ORs* |
| **Table C** | Side-by-side comparison: unadjusted vs adjusted | *Comparison* |

**Rationale for C3 as reference.** C3 Active constructive is the empirically
healthiest profile: highest constructive endorsement (mean top-2 = 0.81 across
6 items), lowest destructive (0.04), highest job satisfaction (median 16.0),
lowest NAQ-frequent (2.7%) and lowest self-labeled bullying (2.7%). Note that C2
carries the hardcoded label "Constructive" in earlier drafts but item-response
probabilities show it has the *lowest* endorsement on all 13 items (constructive
mean 0.08) — it is the **Passive/absent** profile. C3 is the correct healthy
reference for occupational health interpretation.

**Estimator.** Both tables use the same bias-adjusted **ML three-step** estimator
as Part 1 (`ml3step()` from Vermunt, 2010). The measurement model (four-class
general-sample model, 4000 random starts, seed 2125) is loaded from
`lca_results.rds` (produced by Part 1) — no re-fitting is needed here. The
posterior matrix `post4` and modal assignments `modal4` are taken from that saved
object.

**Adjusted model.** The multivariable estimator (`ml3step_multi()`) maximises the
same likelihood as the univariate version but includes all 8 covariates
simultaneously (7 binary + job satisfaction continuous): each OR is conditional
on the remaining seven. Survey weights are
applied throughout. Complete-case analysis is used for the adjusted model (rows
missing any of the 7 covariates are dropped for the structural step only; the
measurement classification matrix D is always computed on the full measurement
sample).

> **Dependency.** Part 3 requires that `lca_results.rds` was written by a recent
> render of Part 1 that includes `post4` (added to the export chunk). If
> `lca_results.rds` predates that edit, re-render Part 1 once first.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| results: "hold"

rm(list = ls()); gc()

required_packages <- c(
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "tibble", "purrr",
  "haven", "readr", "janitor",
  "knitr", "kableExtra"
)
invisible(lapply(required_packages, function(pkg) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages(pkg, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(pkg, character.only = TRUE))
}))

set.seed(2125)
options(scipen = 999)
```

## Load raw data and rebuild analysis frame

The analysis data frame `d_lca` is rebuilt from the raw `.rds` exactly as in
Part 1 (same complete-case filter on 13 items + `sex_woman`). The covariates are
recoded to 0/1 using the same `yes_levels` as Part 1.

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| results: "hold"

resolve_drive_path <- function(rel,
    roots = c("H:/My Drive", "G:/Mi unidad", "C:/Users/andre/Google Drive")) {
  rel <- gsub("\\\\", "/", rel)
  for (r in roots) { p <- file.path(r, rel); if (file.exists(p)) return(p) }
  stop("No se encontro el archivo en ninguna raiz conocida:\n  ",
       paste(file.path(roots, rel), collapse = "\n  "))
}

raw_path <- resolve_drive_path(
  "DOCUMENTOS/6.TESIS 2018/LCA NAQ/BD_2020_input3_match_not_miss.rds")
message("Datos cargados desde: ", raw_path)
raw <- readRDS(raw_path) |> janitor::clean_names()

## ---- variable mapping (identical to Part 1) --------------------------------
items <- paste0("lid_des", c(1:2, 4:14))

as_num <- function(x) {
  if (is.factor(x)) return(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x))))
  as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(x))
}
to01 <- function(x, yes) {
  f <- as.character(haven::as_factor(x))
  f[f %in% c("NA", "Not Apply", "NaN", "")] <- NA
  out <- as.integer(f %in% yes)
  out[is.na(f)] <- NA_integer_
  out
}

## Leadership items: recode to 1-4 factors
d <- raw
item_min <- suppressWarnings(min(vapply(items,
              function(it) min(as.numeric(d[[it]]), na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))))
shift <- if (is.finite(item_min) && item_min == 0) 1L else 0L
for (it in items) d[[it]] <- factor(as.numeric(d[[it]]) + shift, levels = 1:4)
if (shift == 1L) message("Items recodificados de 0-3 a 1-4 (+1).")

## Continuous covariates — same as Part 1's cont_vars
d$job_sat       <- as_num(d[["satis"]])           # job satisfaction sum score (0-20)

## Binary covariates (1 = exposed) — same yes_levels as Part 1
d$sex_woman     <- to01(d[["a52"]],              "Women")
d$eri           <- to01(d[["desbalance_dic"]],   "Yes")
d$naq_frequent  <- to01(d[["naq_a"]],            "2")
d$bully_self    <- to01(d[["autonaq"]],          "Yes")
d$sex_harass    <- to01(d[["acos_sex"]],         "2")
d$auditc_hazard <- to01(d[["auditc"]],           "Yes")
d$no_union      <- to01(d[["org_sind"]],         "Yes")
d$.w            <- as_num(d[["weight"]])

## Complete-case filter: 13 items + sex_woman (concomitant in measurement model)
concomitant <- "sex_woman"
d_lca <- d[stats::complete.cases(d[, c(items, concomitant)]), ]
cat("Rows total:", nrow(d), " | complete on items +", concomitant, ":", nrow(d_lca), "\n")
```

## Helper functions

`class_matrix`, `ml3step`, `ml3step_ref` are identical to Part 1 / Part 2.
`ml3step_multi` is a new multivariable extension.

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| results: "hold"

## Classification matrix D[t, w] = P(W = w | X = t), W = modal class.
class_matrix <- function(post, modal) {
  K   <- ncol(post)
  ind <- outer(modal, 1:K, `==`) * 1
  A   <- t(as.matrix(post)) %*% ind
  A / rowSums(A)
}

## ---- Univariate ML three-step (Vermunt 2010) — ONE covariate z -----------
## Reference class is always class 1 (in the labelling supplied). Returns list
## with $ors tibble(class, OR, lo, hi) for classes 2..K.
ml3step <- function(z, post, modal, sw = NULL, D = NULL) {
  post <- as.matrix(post); K <- ncol(post)
  if (is.null(sw)) sw <- rep(1, nrow(post))
  if (is.null(D))  D  <- class_matrix(post, modal)
  z <- as.numeric(z)
  ok <- !is.na(z)
  z <- z[ok]; modal <- modal[ok]; post <- post[ok, , drop = FALSE]; sw <- sw[ok]
  n <- length(z)
  Dw <- t(D[, modal])                                # n x K
  negll <- function(par) {
    a <- c(0, par[seq(1, 2*(K-1), 2)])
    b <- c(0, par[seq(2, 2*(K-1), 2)])
    eta <- outer(rep(1,n), a) + outer(z, b)
    eta <- eta - apply(eta, 1, max)
    pis <- exp(eta); pis <- pis / rowSums(pis)
    pw  <- rowSums(pis * Dw)
    -sum(sw * log(pmax(pw, 1e-12)))
  }
  fit <- optim(rep(0, 2*(K-1)), negll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
  V   <- tryCatch(solve(fit$hessian),
                  error = function(e) matrix(NA_real_, length(fit$par), length(fit$par)))
  b_idx <- seq(2, 2*(K-1), 2)
  b     <- fit$par[b_idx]
  se    <- sqrt(diag(V))[b_idx]
  list(par = fit$par, V = V, K = K, ors = tibble::tibble(
    class = 2:K, OR = exp(b),
    lo = exp(b - 1.96*se), hi = exp(b + 1.96*se)),
    conv = fit$convergence)
}

## ---- ml3step with an ARBITRARY reference class ----------------------------
## Relabels so `ref` becomes class 1, calls ml3step, maps class indices back.
ml3step_ref <- function(z, post, modal, sw = NULL, ref = 1L) {
  post <- as.matrix(post); K <- ncol(post); ref <- as.integer(ref)
  stopifnot(ref >= 1L, ref <= K)
  ord    <- c(ref, setdiff(seq_len(K), ref))
  postR  <- post[, ord, drop = FALSE]
  modalR <- match(modal, ord)
  m <- ml3step(z = z, post = postR, modal = modalR, sw = sw)
  m$ors$class <- ord[m$ors$class]   # map back to original indices
  m$ref <- ref; m$ord <- ord
  m
}

## ---- Multivariable ML three-step (new for Part 3) -------------------------
## Fits a multinomial logit with ALL p columns of Z simultaneously.
## Z: n x p numeric matrix (or data frame). ref: reference class (default 1).
## D is computed from the FULL measurement sample before listwise deletion on Z.
## Returns $ors tibble(class, covariate, OR, lo, hi), one row per class x covariate.
ml3step_multi <- function(Z, post, modal, sw = NULL, D = NULL, ref = 1L) {
  post <- as.matrix(post); K <- ncol(post); ref <- as.integer(ref)
  stopifnot(ref >= 1L, ref <= K)

  ## Relabel so ref = class 1 (same approach as ml3step_ref)
  ord    <- c(ref, setdiff(seq_len(K), ref))
  postR  <- post[, ord, drop = FALSE]
  modalR <- match(modal, ord)

  if (is.null(sw)) sw <- rep(1, nrow(postR))
  ## D computed on FULL measurement sample BEFORE any covariate filtering
  if (is.null(D))  D  <- class_matrix(postR, modalR)

  if (is.data.frame(Z)) Z <- as.matrix(Z)
  Z  <- apply(Z, 2L, as.numeric)
  p  <- ncol(Z)
  nm <- if (!is.null(colnames(Z))) colnames(Z) else paste0("z", seq_len(p))

  ## Listwise deletion on Z only
  ok      <- complete.cases(Z)
  Zok     <- Z[ok, , drop = FALSE]
  modalOk <- modalR[ok]
  swOk    <- sw[ok]
  n       <- nrow(Zok)

  ## Dw[i, t] = P(W = w_i | X = t) for each complete-case i
  Dw <- t(D[, modalOk])   # n x K

  ## Parameter layout: (K-1) blocks of (1 + p).
  ## Block k (k = 1..K-1, permuted non-reference classes):
  ##   par[(k-1)*(1+p) + 1]        = intercept alpha_{k+1}
  ##   par[(k-1)*(1+p) + 1 + j]    = slope beta_{k+1,j}   (j = 1..p)
  n_par <- (K - 1L) * (1L + p)

  negll <- function(par) {
    ## Intercepts: positions 1, 1+(1+p), 1+2*(1+p), ...
    a <- c(0, par[seq(1L, n_par, by = 1L + p)])   # K intercepts (ref = 0)
    B <- matrix(0, K, p)
    for (k in seq_len(K - 1L)) {
      s <- (k - 1L) * (1L + p) + 2L               # first slope index for class k+1
      B[k + 1L, ] <- par[s:(s + p - 1L)]
    }
    eta <- outer(rep(1, n), a) + Zok %*% t(B)     # n x K
    eta <- eta - apply(eta, 1L, max)
    pis <- exp(eta); pis <- pis / rowSums(pis)
    pw  <- rowSums(pis * Dw)
    -sum(swOk * log(pmax(pw, 1e-12)))
  }

  fit <- optim(rep(0, n_par), negll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)
  V   <- tryCatch(solve(fit$hessian),
                  error = function(e) matrix(NA_real_, n_par, n_par))

  ## Extract OR per non-reference class (permuted) x covariate
  ors <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(K - 1L), function(k) {
    orig_class <- ord[k + 1L]
    s <- (k - 1L) * (1L + p) + 2L
    purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(p), function(j) {
      idx <- s + j - 1L
      b   <- fit$par[idx]
      se  <- if (!anyNA(V)) sqrt(V[idx, idx]) else NA_real_
      tibble::tibble(
        class     = orig_class,
        covariate = nm[j],
        OR        = exp(b),
        lo        = exp(b - 1.96 * se),
        hi        = exp(b + 1.96 * se)
      )
    })
  })

  list(par = fit$par, V = V, K = K, p = p,
       ref = ref, ord = ord, covariate_names = nm,
       ors = ors, conv = fit$convergence,
       n_complete = n, n_total = nrow(Z))
}
```

## Covariate definitions

Seven binary covariates (1 = exposed), matching Part 1's `or_vars`. The reference
class is **C2 Constructive** (index 2 in the four-class model).

```{r}
#| label: covariate-setup
#| results: "hold"

## Reference class: C3 Active constructive — identified by name from class_labels,
## which are canonically derived from item-response profiles in Part 1.
## This lookup is robust to glca class re-ordering across re-renders.
ref_idx <- which(grepl("Active constructive", class_labels))
stopifnot("'Active constructive' class not found in class_labels" = length(ref_idx) == 1L)
cat("Reference class (index", ref_idx, "):", class_labels[ref_idx], "\n")

## Non-reference classes and their display labels
non_ref  <- sort(setdiff(seq_len(K), ref_idx))   # c(1, 3, 4)
col_labs <- paste0(sub("(C\\d+).*", "\\1", class_labels[non_ref]),
                   " vs ", sub("(C\\d+).*", "\\1", class_labels[ref_idx]))
cat("Non-reference classes:", paste(class_labels[non_ref], collapse = "; "), "\n")

## 8 covariates: 7 binary + job satisfaction (continuous, OR per 1-point increase)
or_vars <- c(
  "Effort-reward imbalance"         = "eri",
  "Hazardous alcohol use (AUDIT-C)" = "auditc_hazard",
  "Absence of union"                = "no_union",
  "Frequent negative acts (NAQ)"    = "naq_frequent",
  "Self-labeled bullying"           = "bully_self",
  "Sexual harassment"               = "sex_harass",
  "Female sex"                      = "sex_woman",
  "Job satisfaction (per point)"    = "job_sat"
)

## Sanity check: all covariate columns exist in d_lca
miss <- setdiff(as.character(or_vars), names(d_lca))
if (length(miss)) stop("Missing covariate columns in d_lca: ", paste(miss, collapse=", "))
cat("All", length(or_vars), "covariate columns confirmed in d_lca.\n")
```

# Collinearity diagnostics {#collinearity}

Before the OR tables: a correlation matrix and variance inflation factors (VIFs)
among the 8 covariates. High inter-correlations (especially among ERI, NAQ,
bullying, and job satisfaction) indicate that the adjusted model is partially
residualising shared signal rather than removing clean confounding, which can
destabilise individual coefficients even when the overall fit is good.

```{r}
#| label: collinearity-diag
#| results: "hold"

cov_keys_vec <- as.character(or_vars)   # column names, in or_vars order

## Complete-case matrix for the 8 covariates
Z_diag <- as.matrix(d_lca[, cov_keys_vec])
Z_diag <- apply(Z_diag, 2, as.numeric)
colnames(Z_diag) <- names(or_vars)   # display labels as column names

Z_cc <- Z_diag[complete.cases(Z_diag), ]
cat(sprintf("Collinearity diagnostics on %d complete-case rows.\n", nrow(Z_cc)))

## ---- Pearson correlation matrix ------------------------------------------
## Phi (binary-binary) and point-biserial (binary-continuous) via Pearson r.
cor_mat <- round(cor(Z_cc), 3)

cor_mat |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Covariate") |>
  knitr::kable("markdown",
    caption = paste0(
      "Pearson correlation matrix (phi for binary pairs, point-biserial for binary x ",
      "continuous). Values |r| > 0.40 may inflate VIFs meaningfully; |r| > 0.60 ",
      "indicate severe multicollinearity in the adjusted model."))

## ---- VIF: regress each predictor on the remaining seven ------------------
## VIF_j = 1 / (1 - R^2_j) where R^2_j comes from regressing predictor j on all others.
## Does not depend on the outcome model so applies directly to the ml3step design matrix.
vif_vec <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(Z_cc)), function(j) {
  y      <- Z_cc[, j]
  others <- Z_cc[, -j, drop = FALSE]
  r2     <- tryCatch(
    summary(lm(y ~ others))$r.squared,
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  if (is.na(r2) || r2 >= 1) Inf else 1 / (1 - r2)
}, numeric(1))

vif_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Covariate = names(or_vars),
  `Column`  = cov_keys_vec,
  VIF       = round(vif_vec, 2),
  `Concern` = dplyr::case_when(
    vif_vec >= 10  ~ "Severe (>= 10)",
    vif_vec >= 5   ~ "Moderate (5-10)",
    vif_vec >= 2.5 ~ "Mild (2.5-5)",
    TRUE           ~ "Low (< 2.5)")
)
vif_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(-Column) |>
  knitr::kable("markdown",
    caption = paste0(
      "Variance inflation factors (VIF) for the 8-covariate adjusted model. ",
      "Rule of thumb: VIF < 2.5 = low concern, 2.5-5 = mild, 5-10 = moderate, ",
      ">= 10 = severe. Covariates with high VIF produce unstable adjusted ORs; ",
      "their individual coefficients absorb the shared variance of correlated predictors."))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Interpretation caveat — adjusted job satisfaction OR

Job satisfaction is moderately to strongly correlated with ERI, NAQ, and
self-labeled bullying (all markers of workplace adversity). In the adjusted model
each OR for job satisfaction is **net of** those three covariates, i.e. it
represents the residual satisfaction effect among workers with identical ERI,
NAQ, and bullying exposure. This is a narrow conditioning that may not align
with the construct as described in the manuscript.

Per the manuscript's house-style rule (*"prefer marginal predicted probabilities
for interpretation; ORs are supporting quantities"*), **do not quote the
adjusted job-satisfaction OR in prose** until you have resolved whether (a) VIFs
are acceptable and (b) the coefficient is stable across plausible subsets of the
covariate set. The unadjusted job-satisfaction OR (one covariate at a time) is
the safer interpretable quantity.
:::

# Unadjusted ORs — one covariate at a time, reference = C3 Active constructive {#unadjusted}

One `ml3step_ref()` call per covariate (univariate, survey-weighted). For each
covariate the complete-case n may differ; rows missing the covariate are dropped
from the structural step only (classification matrix D uses the full measurement
sample). Job satisfaction enters as a continuous predictor; the OR represents the
change in odds per **1-point increase** in the sum score (range 0–20).

```{r}
#| label: unadjusted-fits
#| results: "hold"
#| cache: false

unadj_fits <- lapply(or_vars, function(key) {
  ml3step_ref(z   = d_lca[[key]],
              post = post4, modal = modal4,
              sw   = d_lca$.w, ref = ref_idx)
})

## Check convergence
conv_u <- vapply(unadj_fits, function(m) m$conv, integer(1))
if (any(conv_u != 0))
  message("Unadjusted: non-zero convergence for: ",
          paste(names(or_vars)[conv_u != 0], collapse = ", "))

## Per-covariate complete n
n_u <- vapply(or_vars, function(key) sum(!is.na(d_lca[[key]])), integer(1))
cat("Unadjusted n by covariate:\n")
print(data.frame(covariate = names(or_vars), n = n_u))
```

```{r}
#| label: table-unadjusted
#| results: "hold"

fmt <- function(OR, lo, hi) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", OR, lo, hi)

get_unadj <- function(m, cls) {
  r <- m$ors[m$ors$class == cls, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) return("—")
  fmt(r$OR, r$lo, r$hi)
}

tbl_u <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  m <- unadj_fits[[lab]]
  tibble::tibble(
    Covariate  = lab,
    n          = n_u[[lab]],
    `C1 vs C3` = get_unadj(m, 1L),
    `C2 vs C3` = get_unadj(m, 2L),
    `C4 vs C3` = get_unadj(m, 4L)
  )
})

tbl_u |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `C1 Constructive vs C3` = `C1 vs C3`,
    `C2 Passive/absent vs C3` = `C2 vs C3`,
    `C4 Ambivalent vs C3` = `C4 vs C3`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable("markdown",
    caption = paste0(
      "Table U. Unadjusted ML three-step odds ratios (95% CI), reference = C3 Active constructive. ",
      "One covariate at a time; survey-weighted. Binary covariates: OR = odds ratio for ",
      "exposed vs unexposed. Job satisfaction: OR per 1-point increase in the sum score (0-20). ",
      "Classification matrix D fixed from the four-class measurement model ",
      "(Part 1, seed 2125, n.init = ", res$n_init, ")."))
```

*Note.* OR > 1 for a profile Cx vs C3 means that workers in Cx have **higher**
odds of being exposed to that covariate than workers in C3 (Active constructive). OR < 1
means lower odds. Reference profile = C3 Active constructive (the empirically healthiest
leadership pattern).

# Adjusted ORs — all 7 covariates simultaneously, reference = C3 Active constructive {#adjusted}

A single `ml3step_multi()` call with all 8 covariates in the multinomial logit
simultaneously (7 binary + job satisfaction continuous). Each OR is conditional on
the remaining seven. Survey weights applied. Complete-case analysis: rows missing
**any** of the 8 covariates are excluded from the structural step. The job
satisfaction OR is per **1-point increase** in the sum score (0–20).

```{r}
#| label: adjusted-fit
#| results: "hold"
#| cache: false

## Build the 7-column design matrix (n x 7), preserving column names for output
Z_all <- as.matrix(d_lca[, as.character(or_vars)])
colnames(Z_all) <- as.character(or_vars)   # internal names (e.g. "eri")

n_adj <- sum(complete.cases(Z_all))
n_drop <- nrow(d_lca) - n_adj
cat(sprintf("Adjusted analysis: n = %d complete on all 7 covariates (%d dropped, %.1f%%).\n",
            n_adj, n_drop, 100 * n_drop / nrow(d_lca)))

adj_fit <- ml3step_multi(
  Z     = Z_all,
  post  = post4,
  modal = modal4,
  sw    = d_lca$.w,
  ref   = ref_idx
)

cat(sprintf("Convergence code: %d (0 = success)\n", adj_fit$conv))
if (adj_fit$conv != 0)
  warning("Adjusted model did not converge cleanly (code ", adj_fit$conv,
          "). Results should be interpreted with caution.")
```

```{r}
#| label: table-adjusted
#| results: "hold"

get_adj <- function(cls, cov_key) {
  r <- adj_fit$ors[adj_fit$ors$class == cls &
                   adj_fit$ors$covariate == cov_key, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) return("—")
  fmt(r$OR, r$lo, r$hi)
}

tbl_a <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Covariate  = lab,
    `C1 vs C3` = get_adj(1L, key),
    `C2 vs C3` = get_adj(2L, key),
    `C4 vs C3` = get_adj(4L, key)
  )
})

tbl_a |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `C1 Constructive vs C3` = `C1 vs C3`,
    `C2 Passive/absent vs C3` = `C2 vs C3`,
    `C4 Ambivalent vs C3` = `C4 vs C3`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable("markdown",
    caption = sprintf(paste0(
      "Table A. Adjusted ML three-step odds ratios (95%% CI), reference = C3 Active constructive. ",
      "All 8 covariates included simultaneously (7 binary + job satisfaction continuous); ",
      "each OR is adjusted for the remaining seven. Job satisfaction OR = per 1-point increase. ",
      "Survey-weighted. Complete-case n = %d (of %d; %d rows dropped missing any covariate). ",
      "Classification matrix D fixed from the four-class measurement model (Part 1)."),
      adj_fit$n_complete, nrow(d_lca), nrow(d_lca) - adj_fit$n_complete))
```

# Comparison: unadjusted vs adjusted {#comparison}

Side-by-side display. For each covariate × profile, the unadjusted OR is followed
by the adjusted OR (in parentheses) in the same cell, so the effect of mutual
adjustment is immediately visible. Substantial changes from unadjusted to adjusted
indicate confounding among the covariates.

```{r}
#| label: table-comparison
#| results: "hold"

combine_or <- function(u_str, a_str) {
  if (u_str == "—" && a_str == "—") return("—")
  paste0(u_str, "\n(adj: ", a_str, ")")
}

tbl_c <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  m <- unadj_fits[[lab]]
  tibble::tibble(
    Covariate  = lab,
    `C1 Constructive vs C3` = combine_or(get_unadj(m, 1L), get_adj(1L, key)),
    `C2 Passive/absent vs C3` = combine_or(get_unadj(m, 2L), get_adj(2L, key)),
    `C4 Ambivalent vs C3` = combine_or(get_unadj(m, 4L), get_adj(4L, key))
  )
})

tbl_c |>
  knitr::kable("markdown",
    caption = paste0(
      "Table C. Unadjusted vs adjusted ML three-step ORs (95% CI), reference = C3 Active constructive. ",
      "Each cell: unadjusted OR (top) and adjusted OR in parentheses. ",
      "The adjusted model includes all 7 covariates simultaneously. ",
      "Large unadjusted-to-adjusted shifts indicate mutual confounding."))
```

# Export

```{r}
#| label: export
#| results: "hold"

ref_tag <- paste0("refC", ref_idx)
readr::write_csv(tbl_u, paste0("tableU_unadjusted_or_", ref_tag, ".csv"))
readr::write_csv(tbl_a, paste0("tableA_adjusted_or_",   ref_tag, ".csv"))

## Raw numeric values for re-formatting
unadj_raw <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  m <- unadj_fits[[lab]]
  purrr::map_dfr(non_ref, function(cls) {
    r <- m$ors[m$ors$class == cls, ]
    tibble::tibble(Covariate = lab, covariate_key = key,
                   comparison = paste0("C", cls, " vs C3"),
                   class = cls,
                   OR = if (nrow(r)) r$OR else NA_real_,
                   lo = if (nrow(r)) r$lo else NA_real_,
                   hi = if (nrow(r)) r$hi else NA_real_,
                   type = "unadjusted",
                   n = n_u[[lab]])
  })
})

adj_raw <- purrr::imap_dfr(or_vars, function(key, lab) {
  purrr::map_dfr(non_ref, function(cls) {
    r <- adj_fit$ors[adj_fit$ors$class == cls & adj_fit$ors$covariate == key, ]
    tibble::tibble(Covariate = lab, covariate_key = key,
                   comparison = paste0("C", cls, " vs C3"),
                   class = cls,
                   OR = if (nrow(r)) r$OR else NA_real_,
                   lo = if (nrow(r)) r$lo else NA_real_,
                   hi = if (nrow(r)) r$hi else NA_real_,
                   type = "adjusted",
                   n = adj_fit$n_complete)
  })
})

or_values <- dplyr::bind_rows(unadj_raw, adj_raw) |>
  dplyr::arrange(covariate_key, class, type)
readr::write_csv(or_values, paste0("tableUA_or_values_", ref_tag, ".csv"))

cat(sprintf(
  "Wrote:\n  tableU_unadjusted_or_%s.csv (%d rows)\n  tableA_adjusted_or_%s.csv (%d rows)\n  tableUA_or_values_%s.csv (%d rows; both models, numeric)\n",
  ref_tag, nrow(tbl_u), ref_tag, nrow(tbl_a), ref_tag, nrow(or_values)))
```
